label: AH-64D Apache (DCS DTC)
pathSyntax: Dot-separated keys of the .dtc "data" object. "[]" = any array index, "{}" = any object key, each as its own segment (e.g. NAV.Mission_1.Points.WPTHZ.POINTS.[].x, Laser.ChannelsCodes.{}.One). An array is user-extensible only when its section has a "template"; "maxItems"/"minItems"/"fixedLength" bound it. Sections marked hidden cover a whole derived/internal subtree. "display" = {unit, factor}: shown value = stored value * factor.
source: DCS 2.9.30.28738 CoreMods/aircraft/AH-64D/DTC; see native-AH-64D.md and EXPORT-NOTES.md

sections.label: AH-64D Apache cartridge
sections.help: Root of data. type/name/terrain are written by the exporter.

sections.label: Datalink config (placeholder)
sections.help: Always an empty array; the DL CONFIG partition is not implemented. IDM members live in the mission unit's datalinks, not the DTC.

sections.label: HF config (placeholder)
sections.help: Always an empty array; the HF partition is not implemented.

sections.label: NAV: points, routes, tactical graphics, ADF
sections.help: Two mission files (MISSION 1 is loaded by MASTER LOAD; MISSION 2 must be loaded explicitly on the DTU page). Terrain-gated as a whole.

sections.label: Mission 1
sections.help: NAV mission file 1. Loaded by MASTER LOAD.

sections.label: M1 Waypoints / hazards (W/H 01-50)
sections.help: Navigation waypoints (idents 1-6: LZ, CC, PP, RP, SP, WP) and hazards (7-10: towers, wires). Route legs reference these by num 1-50. Filled by the exporter from the planned route. First 25 are the cockpit "safe set".

sections.label: M1 WPTHZ points
sections.help: Max 50. num 1-50, unique within the partition. JSON array, no nulls.

sections.label: M1 Control measures (C51-C99)
sections.help: Friendly/enemy unit symbols and general control measures (BP, AA, FARP, checkpoints...). Route legs may reference them by num 51-99. Avoid C92-C99 (used for datalink present-position reports). User-added.

sections.label: M1 CTRLM points
sections.help: Max 49. num 51-99, unique within the partition. JSON array, no nulls.

sections.label: M1 Targets / threats (T01-T50)
sections.help: Target points (TG) and air-defence threat symbols, each with a cockpit threat ring. Cannot be part of routes. The exporter writes the plan's target-flagged waypoints here (ident TG).

sections.label: M1 TGT points
sections.help: Max 50. num 1-50, unique within the partition. JSON array, no nulls.

sections.label: M1 routes (10)
sections.help: Exactly 10 routes, merged by index. Each leg references a WPTHZ (1-50) or CTRLM (51-99) point number of the same mission. The exporter writes the planned route into route 1.

sections.label: Route legs
sections.help: Up to 99 legs in flight order. The same num may not appear twice in a row. A num that is not an existing WPTHZ/CTRLM point crashes the ME routes page.

sections.label: M1 tactical lines
sections.help: Battlefield lines (boundary, FLOT, phase lines...). Max 15. Entries without type_num/text/vertices or with <2 or >4 vertices are deleted on load.

sections.label: Line vertices
sections.help: 2 to 4 points, in order.

sections.label: M1 engagement areas (EA1-EA12)
sections.help: Engagement areas, labelled EA1..EA12 by index in the cockpit. Max 12.

sections.label: Corners
sections.help: Exactly 4 corners forming a non-self-intersecting quadrilateral (the ME draws axis-aligned rectangles >= 250 m). Any other count deletes the entry.

sections.label: Label positions (derived)
sections.help: Recomputed by the ME on every draw. Write [] but always write the key: a missing caption_pos throws (table.insert on nil).

sections.label: Centre (debug)
sections.help: Debug only; write {"x":0,"y":0} like the ME.

sections.label: M1 fire zones
sections.help: Priority fire zones and no-fire zones; the cockpit can load PF, NF or both.

sections.help: COM presets used by the radios, and preset text messages. Not terrain-gated.

sections.label: COM presets 1-10
sections.help: Exactly 10 presets, merged by index (a partial entry inherits the defaults of the same index). No net members/subscribers here: those are in the mission unit's IDM datalink settings.

sections.label: MPS text messages 1-10
sections.help: Preset free-text messages sent over the datalink. Exactly 10, merged by index.

sections.label: Weapons
sections.help: Hellfire channels and per-crew-station weapon defaults.

sections.label: Laser codes
sections.help: Laser devices and the 16 code letters A-R (no I/O).

sections.label: Laser code letters
sections.help: Keys A B C D E F G H J K L M N P Q R; each a 4-digit code stored as separate digits.

sections.label: MISC: ASE, RLWR, RFI, PERF
sections.help: Survivability equipment, threat tables and performance planning. Not terrain-gated.

sections.label: ASE / CMDS
sections.help: Countermeasure programs and ASE page options. All values are 1-based list indexes, not physical units.

sections.label: RLWR threat table (APR-39 / AVR-2)
sections.help: Array of exactly 96, merged BY INDEX onto the defaults. Keep the default order and leave PRI alone: reordering makes entry i inherit leftover default emitters of entry i. Only display are safe to change.

sections.label: Emitters (derived)
sections.help: Static, from threats_base; copy from the defaults at the same index.

sections.label: RFI threat table (APR-48)
sections.help: Array of exactly 90, merged BY INDEX onto the defaults. Keep the default order and leave PRI alone: reordering makes entry i inherit leftover default emitters of entry i. Only display/hostile/friendly are safe to change. The RFI tab is disabled in this DCS build (it is still saved with its defaults); whether the aircraft reads it is unconfirmed.

sections.label: Emitters (derived)
sections.help: Static, from threats_base; copy from the defaults at the same index.

sections.label: Performance planning
sections.help: PERF page planning values (pressure altitude, temperature, gross weight).

fields.label: Aircraft type
fields.help: Must be exactly "AH-64D_BLK_II". setData checks data.type; anything else returns immediately and the cartridge becomes pure defaults.

fields.label: Cartridge name (cosmetic)
fields.help: Informational; the ME sets it to the export name. The envelope name is what the mission references.

fields.label: Map (terrain id)
fields.help: Mission theatre id. NAV (both missions: points, routes, lines, areas, zones, ADF) imports only when this equals the current map; missing = NAV silently dropped. Everything else imports on any map.

fields.label: Mission file selected when saved
fields.help: Saved by the ME but never read by the descriptor; keep 1.

fields.label: M1 upload WPTHZ points

options.label: No, keep it in the cartridge only (DCS default)

fields.help: "Do not upload tab data" checkbox in the DTC editor, stored NON-inverted as isEnabled: true = the WPTHZ partition is loaded into the aircraft, false (the DCS default) = it is not. A fresh cartridge uploads nothing for this tab until this is true. The exporter sets true when it writes points here.

fields.label: Point number
fields.help: Point index within the partition (WPTHZ 1-50). Must be unique; gaps allowed. Missing num throws in the ME.

fields.label: Ident (symbol)
fields.help: Partition-local ident; default 6. Cockpit Point_ID = id.

fields.label: Free text
fields.help: Up to 3 characters, upper case (the ME upper-cases). Default letter + 2-digit number, e.g. W01 (H for hazard idents 7-10). Empty shows the index in the cockpit.

fields.label: Note (ME only)
fields.help: Mission Editor comment, not uploaded. Write "".

fields.help: DCS map metres, x = north (unit.x in a .miz).

fields.label: Map Y (east)
fields.help: DCS map metres, y = east (unit.y in a .miz).

fields.label: Elevation
fields.help: Point elevation, metres MSL (the ME shows feet; new points default to terrain height). Missing alt throws in the ME grid.

fields.help: Knots (UI "True Airspeed"; manual says ground speed). Default 80. Derived from eta when fix is true.

fields.label: Leg distance (derived)
fields.help: Metres from the previous leg point (0 for the first); see derived[].

fields.label: Leg time
fields.help: Seconds. Legs 2..n: leg duration dist/(speed*0.514). Leg 1: 0 (what the ME converges to). Input when fix is true, derived otherwise.

fields.label: Fix ETA
fields.help: true = the leg is defined by eta and speed is derived; false = eta is derived from speed.
